chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Hakeem narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying:

"Before this matter (the appearance of al-Mahdi), there will be a Biyuh." I did not know what the Biyuh was, so I went for Hajj and heard a nomad saying: "This is a Biyuh day." I asked him: "What is the Biyuh?" He said: "The severe heat."

key_terms.أَعْرَابِيًا: A nomad or Bedouin, used here as a source of linguistic clarification
key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: The matter, referring to the appearance (al-Khuruj) of al-Mahdi
key_terms.الْبِيُوح: A specific term mentioned as a sign before the Mahdi's appearance, explained as extreme heat

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Biyuh' in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) identifies 'Biyuh'—a term of unknown etymology to the narrator—as a specific sign preceding the Mahdi's appearance, later clarified by a Bedouin as a day of intense heat. This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the eschatological significance of climatic anomalies as divine indicators, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition of interpreting natural phenomena as precursors to the Great Revival.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (44) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik from Mo’awiya bin Hakeem that Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abu Nasr had said: “I heard Imam ar-Redha (as) saying: “

Before this matter (the appearance of al-Mahdi) there will be (bayooh).” I did not know the meaning of (bayooh). When I went to offer the hajj, I heard a nomad saying: “This is a (bayooh) day.” I asked him: “What does (bayooh) mean?” He said: “It means very hot.”
